currentContext.strengths: Diversified global network across 22+ countries with 90+ offices and 600+ compliant factory partners, mitigating geographic and customer concentration risk|Asset-light, entrepreneurial operating model combined with an integrated platform spanning design, sourcing, manufacturing and brand management, enabling flexibility while maintaining scale|Design capability at scale via a network of 250+ designers across key fashion hubs, supporting differentiated, commercially-relevant product development|Vendor-consolidation tailwind: global retailers are increasingly partnering with fewer, larger scaled sourcing platforms capable of end-to-end solutions, favouring integrated players like PDS|Deepening presence in the U.S./Americas market through new customer acquisitions and expanded wallet share, a structurally higher-value growth vector
currentContext.strategies: Disciplined build-or-buy capital allocation: businesses incubated internally are funded through the P&L (where there is customer visibility and execution strength), while balance sheet capital is deployed selectively to acquire profitable businesses that bring established operations, differentiated capabilities or access to new markets and customers.|New investments are calibrated within defined Group-level limits linked to profitability, with capital deployment within existing verticals tied to thresholds around PAT and free cash flow, and investment decisions routed through formal governance structures.|Sharper link between performance and ownership: business-head rewards are increasingly linked to profitability, ROCE and working capital management, with pre-defined corrective measures for underperformance to protect the platform from prolonged capital absorption.|Closer oversight through a dedicated Strategy and Growth team working alongside business heads and operational CFOs to track profitability and enable earlier intervention.|Structured, phased 12-month AI roadmap embedding AI across trend intelligence/design, digital product development, sourcing & procurement, manufacturing & logistics, ESG & traceability, and support operations, prioritising high-impact use cases (AI-enabled sourcing, computer vision, design collaboration, enterprise automation).|Manufacturing transformation: evolving owned manufacturing (GoodEarth Apparels and Progress Apparel in Bangladesh, Knit Gallery in India) from standalone factories into an integrated manufacturing platform, aligning customer engagement and operational best practices across units while continuing to operate them as independent profit centres, to drive cost efficiencies as scale increases.|Strategic positioning to benefit from India's rising relevance in global sourcing and from a potential FTA-led demand shift as India-UK and India-EU trade agreements progress, leveraging the Knit Gallery platform.|People strategy built on four pillars (Build, Connect, Develop, Govern) to strengthen leadership pipelines, reduce key-person dependency through succession planning, and build workforce capability to support scale across a complex, multi-entity global platform.|Dividend is paid out of the profits of the financial year under a Board-formulated Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A). The Board declared an interim dividend during the year and recommended a final dividend for shareholder approval, consistent with that policy; no profit was transferred to the general reserve account during the year. The Company has neither invited nor accepted public deposits.
currentContext.expansion: The Manufacturing business transitioned during the year from a standalone factory setup to a more integrated manufacturing arm comprising three facilities: two in Bangladesh and one in India, the latter added through the acquisition of Knit Gallery (Tirupur). On the sourcing side, PDS operates a multi-country network spanning Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Turkey, Vietnam and other emerging regions; Bangladesh remains central to the sourcing base, while capability expansion in India, Vietnam, Egypt and Latin America has widened the sourcing footprint and reduced concentration risk. Capital allocation was deliberately tightened during the year: investment in new verticals was reduced by 27% and capital expenditure was lowered by 56%, reflecting a shift in priority towards profitability, cash generation and returns rather than new capacity build-out.
currentContext.mdna: Retailers are moving beyond single-country sourcing towards diversified, multi-country sourcing networks and consolidating their supplier base with fewer, larger scaled sourcing platforms capable of end-to-end solutions, a structural tailwind for integrated players like PDS.|India, Vietnam and Bangladesh are expected to emerge as key sourcing hubs for US and European apparel brands as China's labour costs have risen sharply, accelerating sourcing diversification; nearshoring is also gaining momentum for Western markets.|Global apparel demand is increasingly value-conscious and inventory-disciplined, with brands shifting from volume-led expansion to profitable, demand-driven growth, and buyers placing smaller, shorter-term orders, which pressures retailer margins but favours agile, technology-enabled sourcing partners.|Inventory correction across the US and European markets is largely complete, with order pipelines strengthening and visibility expected to improve further, alongside gradually recovering discretionary demand and increasing adoption of long-term sourcing partnerships.|Stabilising cotton and other raw-material prices together with easing freight rates are improving supply chain economics for apparel sourcing companies.|Sustainability, traceability and digitalisation are reshaping sourcing decisions, driven by evolving regulatory frameworks (e.g., Extended Producer Responsibility) and growing stakeholder expectations, reinforcing demand for compliant, technology-enabled sourcing partners.|India's Union Budget 2026-27 reinforces government support for the textile and apparel sector (PM MITRA, PLI Scheme for Textiles, National Fibre Scheme, TEEM Scheme, Tex-Eco Initiative, Samarth 2.0), positioning India as a more competitive sourcing destination as brands diversify supply chains.|Key macro/geopolitical risks flagged: ongoing US tariff actions, the Russia-Ukraine conflict, escalating West Asia tensions (energy security, Strait of Hormuz shipping, freight costs), and political instability/labour disruptions in Bangladesh, all of which reshape sourcing patterns and raise logistics/operating costs.|Order book as of early April 2026 increased 11% compared to the same period last year, reflecting healthy demand, deeper customer engagement, and growing momentum in higher-value Sourcing as a Service (SaaS) partnerships.|Growth was led by the UK and Americas, reflecting deepened US market presence through new customer acquisitions and expanded wallet share, while softer demand in Europe and Asia moderated overall performance.

risks.note: Frequent changes in global trade policies and tariff regimes, rising import duties, evolving customs requirements and increased scrutiny of country-of-origin compliance add to sourcing costs and operational complexity, forcing PDS and its customers to restructure sourcing networks and renegotiate supplier contracts.
The global fashion industry is expected to deliver only low single-digit growth in 2026 amid continued macroeconomic uncertainty, with evolving and increasingly value-conscious consumer behaviour.

risks.risk: Cautious, value-driven demand in core US/Europe markets
risks.note: Consumer demand across the US and Europe remains cautious and value-driven, leading retailers to maintain lean inventories and shorter order visibility, which continues to exert pressure on margins.

risks.risk: Wage inflation across key sourcing markets
risks.note: Wage inflation across key sourcing markets remains a structural cost challenge, reinforcing the need for diversified sourcing strategies and disciplined cost management.

risks.risk: Margin compression from new-vertical investments and one-off costs
risks.note: Operating profit margin declined to 2.7% from 3.1% and net profit margin moderated to 1.4% from 1.9% in FY 2024-25, primarily due to losses from new vertical investments, one-time restructuring and redundancy costs, and higher licence-related expenses; return on capital employed also declined to 18.0% from 19.3%.

risks.risk: Concentration on a single unified digital backbone
risks.note: A unified SAP S/4HANA backbone governs over 150 legal entities across 22+ countries; a failure, disruption or cybersecurity breach in this centralised system could have enterprise-wide operational impact.

risks.risk: Complexity of a large, decentralised multi-entity structure
risks.note: The organisational structure comprises multiple legal entities including numerous subsidiaries, joint ventures and associate companies operating under an entrepreneurial, profit-and-loss-delegated model, which increases governance and internal-control complexity even as it preserves operational independence.

thesis: Asset-light global apparel sourcing platform navigating a tough FY26 (cautious consumers, tariff turbulence, retailer inventory discipline). Delivered modest top-line growth (GMV +5%, Rev +4%) but EBITDA/PAT declined YoY on restructuring/redundancy one-offs and new-vertical drag. Core thesis intact and arguably strengthening structurally: retailers under cost pressure are outsourcing design + sourcing operations (sourcing-as-a-service / SaaS), and PDS + Li & Fung are the only credible global players at RFQ stage. Balance sheet materially de-levered (net debt ₹374cr → ~₹105cr; NWC 17d → 4d). FY27 framed as "restoration of profitability" year (cautious mid-single-digit revenue, ~10% PAT growth), then mid-teens medium-term growth. Order book +11% (Americas +30%) gives FY27 visibility. Brands the one weak/under-review segment.
scorecard (fy26):
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GMV | ~₹19,666 cr | ~₹18,730 cr | **+5%** | ~$2.22bn; ~0.1% of $1.9trn global apparel mkt; targeting ~₹20,000cr GMV FY27 |
| Revenue | ₹13,110 cr | ~₹12,606 cr | **+4%** | Modest, value-led market; growth led by mfg + Americas momentum |
| Gross margin | 20.6% | 20.1% | **+48 bps** | Procurement efficiency, disciplined sourcing, some Q3 one-offs |
| EBITDA | ₹385 cr | ₹457 cr | **−16%** | Down on restructuring/redundancy one-offs + brand royalty obligations + new-vertical drag |
| PAT (reported) | ₹178 cr | ₹241 cr | **−26%** | Q4 PAT ₹72cr (+95% QoQ vs ₹37cr Q3) on operating leverage + lower finance cost |
| Other income | ₹99.7 cr | ~₹50 cr | ~2x | FX gains + ~₹19cr MTM on PDS Ventures investments |
| Finance cost | ₹146.5 cr | ~₹126 cr | +16% | Like-for-like ex-Knit Gallery only +3%; −5.4% QoQ |
| Net debt | ~₹105 cr | ₹374 cr | **−72%** | Despite ~₹91cr debt consolidated from Knit Gallery acquisition |
| Net debt/EBITDA | ~0.27x | — | — | Comfortable leverage |
| Norm. ROCE | ~25% | — | — | Improving capital efficiency |
| NWC days | 4 | 17 | −13d | Ex-New Lobster, core sourcing+mfg ~0 or slightly negative days |
| OCF | ~₹781 cr | — | — | Strong; capex >50% lower YoY |
| ETR | 13.5% | 10.1% | — | Full Pillar-2 impact now in ETR; Q4 ETR ~7.9% (DTA on ₹14cr DBS Lifestyle impairment + losses) |

**Call-outs:** (a) **US tariff** turbulence dented Krayons (US-focused) in H2; Americas Q4 top-line ~flat (+0.4% $); but order book +30%. (b) **Customer mix** — top-10 clients expected to grow only ~7-8% (below 11% OB avg); 2 of top-10 had "a lot of challenges" in FY26; growth to be led by new verticals + North America. (c) **JV/one-offs** — Knit Gallery (mfg) + GSCL/Michael Lee (sourcing) acquisitions inflated opex/employee/finance cost; redundancy/restructuring provisions, brand royalty obligations, ₹14cr DBS Lifestyle impairment, closures (Lilly & Sid, Design ARC branch, Grupo, J-Craft).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue growth FY27:** mid-single-digit (5-6%), deliberately cautious vs 11% order book (customers pushing back shipments / inventory caution).
- **PAT/profit growth FY27:** ~10% ("close to about 10% plus broad growth in profits").
- **Gross margin:** +40-50 bps per year over next 1-2 years (reiterated from Q3 call).
- **EBITDA margin:** +50-75 bps (slightly more than GM, as one-time restructuring costs roll off).
- **Opex discipline:** growth in employee + other expenses to stay **below top-line growth**.
- **New-vertical investment:** down 27% in FY26; target ~₹80cr in FY27 (from ₹165cr FY25); ~₹50-60cr/yr recurring thereafter. No new verticals/investments for next 12 months.
- **Medium/long term:** mid-teens revenue growth ("historically achieved"); aspires to 5% PAT margin ("the 555") — acknowledged behind on this.
- **Order book (early Apr):** ~₹5,074 cr, +11% YoY. Americas +30%; Asia +8-9%; UK/Europe +3-4%.
- **Dividend:** ₹3.3/share proposed (₹1.65 interim already paid); ~42% of FY26 PAT.
order book / pipeline:
- Order book ~₹5,074cr, +11% YoY (Apr). North America +~30%.
- New SaaS mandate signed with a **leading US value retailer**, potential to scale beyond **~₹475 cr** over time.
- ~5 strategic partnerships now established across US retailer/brand ecosystem ("green shoots").
- Healthy SaaS traction building in **UK & Europe** too.
- **Large SaaS contracts in pipeline** — active conversations with retailers wanting PDS to take over their Asia sourcing offices/headcount; "large contract signed" expected in next 2-3 months; typically **4-5 year contracts** (predictable revenue/bottom line).
- One of largest **French supermarkets** (becoming food-first) in discussions to divest entire Asia sourcing to PDS via SaaS.
- Global source contracts at RFQ stage: only PDS and **Li & Fung** in final contention.
segment view:
| Segment | FY26 Rev | EBIT / margin | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sourcing** (design-led + SaaS) | ~₹12,399 cr | EBIT ₹266 cr | Resilient core; design-led GM 15-18%; ~600 approved factories across Asia; vendor-of-record for Primark, Kohl's |
| **Manufacturing** | ~₹1,034 cr | EBIT ₹57 cr (~5.5%) | **+31% YoY**; own factories Bangladesh/Sri Lanka/India; helped by Knit Gallery integration + better utilization |
| **Brands & IP** | (in above) | Loss-making/under review | Ted Baker (New Lobster) the big pain point; wholesale challenged; rationalizing portfolio |

Four service lines articulated: (1) Manufacturing (own factories), (2) Strategic vendor / design-led sourcing, (3) Agency / sourcing-as-a-service, (4) Brands. First three confident & profitable; brands under evaluation.
growth / optionality:
- **SaaS (sourcing-as-a-service)** is the key optionality — retailers cutting overheads & outsourcing Asia sourcing ops to PDS; long 4-5yr contracts; PDS one of only two global credible players.
- **US near-shoring / new accounts** — Americas OB +30%, ~5 strategic US partnerships, Walmart relationship (retailers source 70-80% via third parties, not own offices).
- **New verticals maturing** — of ~20 new verticals started over 3 yrs, 12-13 now profitable; expected to scale next 2-3 yrs.
- **PDS Ventures** — tech portfolio at improving value realization, moving to self-sustaining (new investments only from exit cash).
- Design-led sourcing tailwind: retailers reducing in-house design teams.
margins & cost:
- GM +48bps to 20.6% FY26; guided +40-50bps/yr.
- Q4 sequential opex improvement: employee cost flat QoQ, other expenses −6% QoQ.
- Employee cost ₹1,317cr (vs ₹1,211cr); ex-Knit Gallery/GSCL like-for-like only +3-3.5% (~₹40cr). New base ₹1,310cr.
- Other expenses +16% YoY headline; ex-acquisitions ~+11%; one-offs = brand royalty obligations (couldn't cut despite brand curtailment) + shutdown provisions.
- **Project PULSE** — BCG-led cost transformation now institutionalized; AI-enabled digital backbone (procurement, supplier governance, pricing intelligence, MDM). Expected ~₹40-50cr/yr procurement savings + similar in opex.
- Poeticgem & Simple Approach saw PBT margin erosion from one-time redundancy costs (BCG manpower rationalization in H2); expected to bounce back.
capex: - FY26 capex reduced by **>50% YoY** — disciplined capital allocation, asset-light model. No major capex flagged for FY27.
capital allocation:
- Net debt cut to ~₹105cr (from ₹374cr); net debt/EBITDA ~0.27x.
- OCF ~₹781cr; NWC at 4 days.
- New-vertical investment curtailed (−27%; target ₹80cr FY27); no new investments next 12 months.
- PDS Ventures self-funding from exits only.
- Dividend ₹3.3/share (~42% payout) — track record maintained.
- Active portfolio rationalization: closed Lilly & Sid, Design ARC branch; consolidated Design ARC Asia + licensing into Poeticgem; exited Grupo, J-Craft; ₹14cr impairment DBS Lifestyle.
risks:
- **US demand / tariff** — Krayons (US-focused) declined H2 on tariff turbulence; Americas Q4 ~flat.
- **Customer concentration** — top-10 to grow only ~7-8%; 2 of top-10 challenged in FY26.
- **Demand caution / shipment pushback** — customers deferring shipments, inventory caution → OB-to-revenue conversion gap (11% OB vs 5-6% rev guide).
- **Brands / Ted Baker (New Lobster)** — agency sales hit by franchisee bankruptcies (ABG-appointed); GM fell ~30%→20%; outcome hinges on ABG financial contribution ($2-2.5m/yr, only 12 months committed) or new retail partner — decision in 4-6 weeks.
- **Working capital** — mgmt commits to hold ~4 days but flags QoQ fluctuation risk from US/Europe expansion & logistics.
- New-vertical gestation drag (12-24 months) until maturity.
mgmt tone: Cautious-but-confident / candid. Repeatedly emphasized "extreme caution" for FY27 amid macro/geopolitical/tariff uncertainty, while stressing structural strengthening (leaner, de-levered, disciplined). Frank admission: "we are not happy with the last 18-24 months performance"; behind on 5% PAT target. Constructive on SaaS/US optionality and de-leveraging. Brands acknowledged as a "mixed success."
non-obvious points:
- **SaaS contracts are 4-5yr, predictable** — structurally different from quarterly transactional sourcing; reduces revenue volatility if signed.
- Retailers source only **15-20% via own offices, 70-80% via third parties** — structural runway for design-led sourcing (Walmart context).
- Only **PDS + Li & Fung** at final RFQ for global source contracts — effective duopoly in large outsourced-sourcing deals.
- French supermarket "food-first" pivot → wants to divest entire Asia sourcing — illustrates the SaaS opportunity pipeline.
- New Lobster economics: revenue +4% to ~₹500cr but GM 30%→20% (agency business "dried away"); yet PAT rose ₹13cr→₹38cr.
- Q4 ETR distorted to 7.9% by DTA on DBS Lifestyle impairment + losses (full-year 13.5% with Pillar-2).
- Selfridges concession + Aditya Birla planning 10 more Ted Baker stores in India — brand consumer-connect intact despite wholesale model issues.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ **PDS itself** is a structural beneficiary of retailer cost-cutting / sourcing-office divestment (China+1, vendor consolidation, Asia ops outsourcing).
- ✅ Manufacturing beneficiary of factory consolidation (top-5 factories per country win share; Knit Gallery integration).
- (Direct third-party beneficiaries beyond PDS group: not specifically called out.)

FY26 GMV ₹19,666cr (+5%), Rev ₹13,110cr (+4%), EBITDA ₹385cr (−16%), PAT ₹178cr (−26%). Net debt ₹374→₹105cr. OB ₹5,074cr (+11%; Americas +30%). New ~₹475cr US SaaS mandate. Guidance FY27: mid-single-digit rev, ~10% PAT, GM +40-50bps, opex < top-line, new-vertical invest ₹80cr. Dividend ₹3.3/sh. New base: employee cost ₹1,310cr. Project PULSE (BCG/AI cost transformation) institutionalized.

| **Manufacturing** | ~₹1,034 cr | EBIT ₹57 cr (~5.5%) | **+31% YoY**; own factories Bangladesh/Sri Lanka/India; helped by Knit Gallery integration + better utilization |
| **Brands & IP** | (in above) | Loss-making/under review | Ted Baker (New Lobster) the big pain point; wholesale challenged; rationalizing portfolio |

Four service lines articulated: (1) Manufacturing (own factories), (2) Strategic vendor / design-led sourcing, (3) Agency / sourcing-as-a-service, (4) Brands. First three confident & profitable; brands under evaluation.
growth / optionality:
- **SaaS (sourcing-as-a-service)** is the key optionality — retailers cutting overheads & outsourcing Asia sourcing ops to PDS; long 4-5yr contracts; PDS one of only two global credible players.
- **US near-shoring / new accounts** — Americas OB +30%, ~5 strategic US partnerships, Walmart relationship (retailers source 70-80% via third parties, not own offices).
- **New verticals maturing** — of ~20 new verticals started over 3 yrs, 12-13 now profitable; expected to scale next 2-3 yrs.
- **PDS Ventures** — tech portfolio at improving value realization, moving to self-sustaining (new investments only from exit cash).
- Design-led sourcing tailwind: retailers reducing in-house design teams.
margins & cost:
- GM +48bps to 20.6% FY26; guided +40-50bps/yr.
- Q4 sequential opex improvement: employee cost flat QoQ, other expenses −6% QoQ.
- Employee cost ₹1,317cr (vs ₹1,211cr); ex-Knit Gallery/GSCL like-for-like only +3-3.5% (~₹40cr). New base ₹1,310cr.
- Other expenses +16% YoY headline; ex-acquisitions ~+11%; one-offs = brand royalty obligations (couldn't cut despite brand curtailment) + shutdown provisions.
- **Project PULSE** — BCG-led cost transformation now institutionalized; AI-enabled digital backbone (procurement, supplier governance, pricing intelligence, MDM). Expected ~₹40-50cr/yr procurement savings + similar in opex.
- Poeticgem & Simple Approach saw PBT margin erosion from one-time redundancy costs (BCG manpower rationalization in H2); expected to bounce back.
capex: - FY26 capex reduced by **>50% YoY** — disciplined capital allocation, asset-light model. No major capex flagged for FY27.
capital allocation:
- Net debt cut to ~₹105cr (from ₹374cr); net debt/EBITDA ~0.27x.
- OCF ~₹781cr; NWC at 4 days.
- New-vertical investment curtailed (−27%; target ₹80cr FY27); no new investments next 12 months.
- PDS Ventures self-funding from exits only.
- Dividend ₹3.3/share (~42% payout) — track record maintained.
- Active portfolio rationalization: closed Lilly & Sid, Design ARC branch; consolidated Design ARC Asia + licensing into Poeticgem; exited Grupo, J-Craft; ₹14cr impairment DBS Lifestyle.
risks:
- **US demand / tariff** — Krayons (US-focused) declined H2 on tariff turbulence; Americas Q4 ~flat.
- **Customer concentration** — top-10 to grow only ~7-8%; 2 of top-10 challenged in FY26.
- **Demand caution / shipment pushback** — customers deferring shipments, inventory caution → OB-to-revenue conversion gap (11% OB vs 5-6% rev guide).
- **Brands / Ted Baker (New Lobster)** — agency sales hit by franchisee bankruptcies (ABG-appointed); GM fell ~30%→20%; outcome hinges on ABG financial contribution ($2-2.5m/yr, only 12 months committed) or new retail partner — decision in 4-6 weeks.
- **Working capital** — mgmt commits to hold ~4 days but flags QoQ fluctuation risk from US/Europe expansion & logistics.
- New-vertical gestation drag (12-24 months) until maturity.
mgmt tone: Cautious-but-confident / candid. Repeatedly emphasized "extreme caution" for FY27 amid macro/geopolitical/tariff uncertainty, while stressing structural strengthening (leaner, de-levered, disciplined). Frank admission: "we are not happy with the last 18-24 months performance"; behind on 5% PAT target. Constructive on SaaS/US optionality and de-leveraging. Brands acknowledged as a "mixed success."
non-obvious points:
- **SaaS contracts are 4-5yr, predictable** — structurally different from quarterly transactional sourcing; reduces revenue volatility if signed.
- Retailers source only **15-20% via own offices, 70-80% via third parties** — structural runway for design-led sourcing (Walmart context).
- Only **PDS + Li & Fung** at final RFQ for global source contracts — effective duopoly in large outsourced-sourcing deals.
- French supermarket "food-first" pivot → wants to divest entire Asia sourcing — illustrates the SaaS opportunity pipeline.
- New Lobster economics: revenue +4% to ~₹500cr but GM 30%→20% (agency business "dried away"); yet PAT rose ₹13cr→₹38cr.
- Q4 ETR distorted to 7.9% by DTA on DBS Lifestyle impairment + losses (full-year 13.5% with Pillar-2).
- Selfridges concession + Aditya Birla planning 10 more Ted Baker stores in India — brand consumer-connect intact despite wholesale model issues.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ **PDS itself** is a structural beneficiary of retailer cost-cutting / sourcing-office divestment (China+1, vendor consolidation, Asia ops outsourcing).
- ✅ Manufacturing beneficiary of factory consolidation (top-5 factories per country win share; Knit Gallery integration).
- (Direct third-party beneficiaries beyond PDS group: not specifically called out.)

---
qoq log: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Q4 PAT ₹72cr (+95% QoQ vs ₹37cr Q3); Americas Q4 ~flat (+0.4% $, −4-5% QoQ) vs 9M US growth ~19% — implied Q4 US softness on tariffs. FY26 GMV ₹19,666cr (+5%), Rev ₹13,110cr (+4%), EBITDA ₹385cr (−16%), PAT ₹178cr (−26%). Net debt ₹374→₹105cr. OB ₹5,074cr (+11%; Americas +30%). New ~₹475cr US SaaS mandate. Guidance FY27: mid-single-digit rev, ~10% PAT, GM +40-50bps, opex < top-line, new-vertical invest ₹80cr. Dividend ₹3.3/sh. New base: employee cost ₹1,310cr. Project PULSE (BCG/AI cost transformation) institutionalized.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
